about: Workshop Journey content. The page at /journey reads this file and workshop/chapters/*.json. Ticks people make are keyed to the position of each done_when item, so rewording keeps them and reordering resets them. Zava, Inc. is fictitious and all figures are synthetic: see docs/synthetic-data.md.

abbreviations.BRD: Business requirements document: the business case. Goals with numbers, who owns each assumption, what is in and out of scope. Written in chapter 04 with BRD Builder.
abbreviations.PRD: Product requirements document: what the product must do, as requirements and acceptance cases you can test. Written in chapter 05 with PRD Builder.
abbreviations.RAI: Responsible AI: checking that an AI feature is fair, safe, transparent and has a person accountable for it. Here, the store assistant.
abbreviations.RPI: Research, plan, implement and review: HVE Core's workflow for making a code change with evidence at every step. Chapter 08.
abbreviations.ADR: Architecture decision record: a short note of one design decision, the options considered and why this one was chosen.
abbreviations.DT: Design Thinking: finding the real problem by talking to the people who have it, before deciding on a fix. Chapter 03.
abbreviations.HVE: Hypervelocity Engineering: Microsoft's approach to AI-assisted software delivery. HVE Core is its open-source set of agents and skills for GitHub Copilot.
abbreviations.PR: Pull request: a proposed change on a branch, opened for review before it is merged into main.

outcome.title: The Silent Night, in three days
outcome.story: One morning every freezer in Zava's five pilot stores is warm, and the only alarms all night were for other cases. Over three days your team finds out why, decides what to fix, builds it with HVE Core and proves it on nights nobody has seen.
outcome.statement: Cut the Cost of a Silent Night without breaking routine operations.
outcome.measure: Euros protected on hidden nights in the Night Gauntlet, against the trainer's baseline for the same seed.
outcome.must_not_change: A scheduled defrost that ends on time raises no alarm.

three-day.what: Replay silent-night at ×60 and walk Business impact. Stop on the newspaper at 08:00.
Check the pre-work: tests pass, HVE Core is installed, Session Target says Copilot, each table has a branch.
Break
Methods 1 and 2: scope the problem, then interview the five characters.
Lunch
Method 3: synthesis, the problem statement and the exit 1 handoff.
Break
BRD Builder: Discover, Define and Govern.
Executives agree the outcome, how it's measured and who owns each assumption.
Recap: each table reads its business goal aloud.
PRD Builder: acceptance cases for each failure, including the case that must not change.
Break
Security Planner and RAI Planner, split by table.
Lunch
functional-planner: from the PRD to work items.
backlog-manager: each table commits to one fix and makes its branch.
Break
Repo rules with hve-builder, then rpi-research on the table's fix.
Every table has research marked ready.
rpi-plan with its critique. Failing tests first.
Break
rpi-implement, one phase at a time. Every existing test still passes.
Lunch
rpi-review and code-review. Then the trainer announces the seed and tables run the Night Gauntlet.
Pull requests, scorecards and the leaderboard, then the Investment Board.
Break
A chaos card hits the funded portfolio. Incident record, runbook change and a hotfix if needed.
Debrief and case file reveal.

one-day.what: Replay silent-night at ×60 and let the room watch the Cost of a Silent Night climb. Stop at 08:00 on the newspaper.
Interviews with the five characters. Find the problem, not the fix.
Agree the outcome and its measure. Executives move the assumption sliders.
Break. Form one table per failure: alarms, commands, identity, assistant, ownership. This replaces chapters 06 and 07.
Each table: acceptance cases with PRD Builder, then Security Planner or RAI Planner for its failure.
Repo rules, then rpi-research, rpi-plan and rpi-implement on each table's branch.
rpi-review against the table's acceptance cases.
Announce the seed. Tables run the Night Gauntlet and hand in scorecards.
Break. The trainer checks every scorecard qualified or knows why not.
Investment Board: three minutes per table, then fund, then the store assistant decision. Play chaos cards during demonstrations: this is chapter 11 in the one-day format.
